It wasn't particularly meaningful. I used to run by a handle that included the words "soap on a rope". I got that username not from bath soap, but from Soap MacTavish of the Modern Warfare series. See, there's a trophy in Modern Warfare 2 that you earn for beating "The Gulag", a campaign mission. At the end of the chapter, you grab a rope and ascend out of the collapsing prison alongside Soap. Hence, "soap on a rope". After seeing that, I put some arbitrary numbers on the end of it and made it my Playstation Network tag. It stayed that way for years, until one day, I decided that I preferred one-word, distinct Internet names after being tactical nuked by some CoD god (in my young eyes) by the name of "Soario". In a perfect world, I could have changed my name to "Rope", and that would have satisfied the need. (Soap was too similar to Mr. MacTavish for my tastes) However, as any netizen worth their salt knows...names like that are absolutely impossible to grab anywhere. So, after some moping, I decided that I'd just add an "n" to the end, and say it out loud. "Ropen", I said. "Now that might just work." Indeed, it did. It's just unusual enough to not have already been registered in most places, and perfectly distinct as I like it. Now, here I am. I don't see it ever changing. I have other names that I use sometimes, but they're always secondary. Ropen is definitely the one true alter ego for me.

I also use a standardized one-word unique name, although while I do have that account on voat already, I'm personally trying out a new (unrelated to previous) name myself as a clean slate of sorts here.
